names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 17 mai, «Sfântul Apostol Andronic și soția sa, Iunia».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 17 Μαΐου, «Άγιοι Ανδρόνικος και Ιουνία οι Απόστολοι», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог's heading for 17. мај ст. ст., „Свети апостол Андроник.“ Свети is not a rank; апостол is the `apostle` this folder carries in `types`; strip them and the bare forename is left, and the heading offers nothing else — the Pannonia, the kinship and the martyrdom are all in the body. **A deliberate exact-form fold, measured with `foldchk.py` before drafting**: `andronicus-of-antioch` already carries „Андроник“ as its **`ru`** form, so the collision is across two languages that spell the name identically. Two men: a companion of Junia among the Seventy, bishop in Pannonia, against a martyr of Antioch. The fold is read in this batch's commit message.

feast.note: Doxologia keeps him twice: its calendar prints him on 17 mai and again on 30 iulie — «Sfinții Apostoli Sila, Silvan, Crescent, Epenet și Andronic». One attestation row per church is the schema, so the row is the day this folder was read from and the second day is recorded here. The 30 iulie line is the common commemoration of the five apostles. Read 25 September 2026.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 17 mai — «Sfântul Apostol Andronic și soția sa, Iunia»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 17ης Μαΐου — «Άγιοι Ανδρόνικος και Ιουνία οι Απόστολοι»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 17 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same civil day the Romanian calendar already keeps him on, and it is plainly the same man: Paul's kinsman and fellow prisoner of Romans 16.7, kept with Junia. **One page carries both of them**, with «Αγιος Ανδρονικος ο Αποστολος» and «Αγια Ιουνια η Αποστολος» as its two head names, so the pair are two upgrades and not one. **The Greek sends him to two other days and neither is taken as a feast**: «Περισσότερες πληροφορίες για τον Άγιο Ανδρόνικο μπορείτε να διαβάσετε στις 30 Ιουλίου», which is the same 30 July the corpus's Romanian row already records as his second doxologia day and is a cross-reference to more reading rather than a second Greek feast; and it counts both apostles among the Seventy, «τους οποίους εορτάζουμε στις 4 Ιανουαρίου», which is the common commemoration of the Seventy and not his own day. One row per church is the schema, so both are recorded here and nothing is moved. **Two apolytikia stand on the page and only the joint one is taken**: the first, Τὸν τάφον σου Σωτὴρ, names Andronicus and Junia together and is copied; the Έτερον in Ἦχος γ’, «Ἀπόστολοι Ἅγιοι, πρεσβεύσατε», is the bare common of apostles and is left. Neither is a mis-hang. **No year is printed**, so no `dates` object is added.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 30.05.2026 (17. мај ст. ст.) — „Свети апостол Андроник.“

attestations.note: The day's first entry, on the same menologion 17/5 the Romanian and Greek rows already carry, so nothing moved. **THE SEE IS SETTLED, AND IT IS THE FIND OF THIS ENTRY.** This folder's own life records that „Andronicus was bishop in Panania, **as doxologia's life spells the place**“ — a spelling the earlier reader would not correct and could not place. The Prologue reads „Андроник би постављен за епископа Паноније“ and then „проповедаше Јеванђеље по целој Панонији“, twice and in two cases: **Pannonia**. Doxologia's Panania is a corruption of it. **The `office` field is still empty and this reader did not fill it**, because `upgrade.py` has no key for `office` and a hand-edit is not sanctioned — **so the one thing this reading licenses is the author's, in one commit: `office: "Bishop of Pannonia"` on a folder that already carries `bishop` in `types`.** **And the same sentence narrows doxologia's claim.** That page makes him „a preacher and teacher … not of one city or one country only but of the whole world“; the Prologue says he did not live in one place but preached the Gospel **through the whole of Pannonia**. The added paragraph says both and chooses neither. **New besides**: that **both of them had the gracious power of wonderworking**, by which they drove demons out of men and healed every infirmity and every sickness — the corpus's life had the healings off doxologia but not the gift named; and that **both suffered for Christ and so received a double crown, of apostleship and of martyrdom**, which is the same reading doxologia's „common debt of nature“ sentence carries. The finding of the relics „у пределима Евгенијским (в. 22. фебруар)“ is the same relic-finding the folder already records from doxologia, and **it is a feast and not a row** — the cross-reference to 22 February is the Prologue's own and no second commemoration is written. **`paul-the-apostle` IS ADDED to `related`.** „Сродник апостола Павла, као што сам Павле пише (Рм 16, 7)“ is **a kinship the body narrates**, which is the test that owes a row, and Paul has a folder; the corpus's life already quoted the verse without the row. `types` untouched — апостол is the `apostle` and „би постављен за епископа“ the `bishop`, both held, and Пострадаше the `martyr`. No `locations`. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Sfinţilor Apostoli rugaţi pe milostivul Dumnezeu ca să dea iertare de greşeli sufletelor noastre.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfinților Apostoli Andronic și al soției sale Iunia», Glasul 3 — the one troparion the page prints for the two together, in the short form of the common of apostles

english.text: Holy apostles, entreat the merciful God to grant our souls forgiveness of our sins.

hymns.text: Δυὰς φωτοειδής, ἱερῶν Ἀποστόλων, καὶ κήρυκες Χριστοῦ, ἀνεδείχθητε κόσμω, τοὶς πάσι κατασπείραντες, τὸ τῆς χάριτος κήρυγμα, ὅθεν σήμερον, ἠμᾶς πιστῶς εὐφημοῦμεν, ὢ Ἀνδρόνικε, καὶ Ἰουνία θεόφρον, Χριστὸν μεγαλύνοντες.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Τὸν τάφον σου Σωτὴρ, on the page of Άγιοι Ανδρόνικος και Ιουνία οι Απόστολοι — the joint hymn of the two; the page gives it no tone line of its own, so none is recorded

english.text: A pair full of light, holy apostles and heralds of Christ, you were shown forth to the world, sowing among all the preaching of grace; and so today we faithfully praise you, O Andronicus and God-minded Junia, magnifying Christ.
